newsitem.title: USA: Hilton targets 25 pct annual EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Hilton targets 25 pct annual EPS growth.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp is targeting annual earnings and EBITDA growth of 25 percent, chief financial officer Matthew Hart said.

He said a key factor contributing to that overall growth rate would be "dependable growth" in its full service hotel segment, where Hilton sees no new supply coming on for the next several years. He also cited the recent Bally acquisition and the several new casino projects it has in development.
Hart also provided cash flow forecasts by division and said that 1996 proforma EBITDA in its hotel segment is expected to grow to $375 million from $301 million last year.
Proforma EBITDA should rise to $295 million in 1996 from $264 million last year at the gaming division; and to $330 million from $267 million at the newly acquired Bally unit.

Hart said the company aimed to build its hotel division through the acquisition of full service hotels from owners such as banks and insurance companies, who are "not natural owners of hotels." Hilton's goal in such acquisitions was to pay 60 to 70 percent of the replacement costs and generate a 10 percent cash-on-cash return in the first year of operation.
